data.title: Rezolute: Advancing Ersodetug Clinical Program and Strong Cash Position Underpin Jason McCarthy’s Buy Rating and $14 Price Target
data.description:
Rezolute, the Healthcare sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Jason McCarthy from Maxim Group reiterated a Buy rating on the stock and has a $14.00 price target.

Jason McCarthy has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, primarily the advancing clinical profile of ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism and Rezolute’s financial strength. The Phase 3 upLIFT trial has fully enrolled, builds on strong Expanded Access data, and early patient results show meaningful reductions in IV glucose needs with a favorable safety profile, which increases confidence in upcoming topline data.

In addition, the company’s cash position of about $107.8M is expected to fund operations into 2028, reducing near‑term financing risk. While the prior CHI Phase 3 study missed endpoints, subsequent FDA interactions, including the recommendation for a pre‑BLA meeting, suggest a viable regulatory path that could encompass both tumor HI and CHI. Coupled with derisked revenue assumptions and a $14 price target, McCarthy sees further upside and continued share momentum, supporting his Buy recommendation.

data.title: Kaleon: Buy Rating Backed by Strategic Lake Maggiore Acquisition to Build Integrated Tourism Platform
data.description:
Alessio Olmi, an analyst from TP ICAP MIDCAP, maintained the Buy rating on Kaleon S.p.A.. The associated price target is €5.50.

Alessio Olmi has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, starting with Kaleon’s strategic move to deepen its presence along the visitor journey through the acquisition of an 80% stake in the Lake Maggiore passenger transport operator. This transaction strengthens Kaleon’s transition from a heritage-site manager to an integrated tourism platform capable of internalizing more stages of tourist spending.

The valuation of the acquired business, at an EV of about €2.0mn for expected 2025 sales of €0.8mn, appears attractive relative to Kaleon’s scale and supports earnings accretion over time, particularly as consolidation progresses beyond 2026. While the initial financial contribution is limited, the deal bolsters diversification, opens scope for bundled offers for tour operators, and is expected to be slightly supportive for margins, underpinning the positive view on Kaleon’s medium‑term growth and profitability profile.

data.title: Fiera Capital Kept at Hold as Organic Growth Challenges and Elevated Leverage Prompt Price Target Cut to $5
data.description:
Fiera Capital A, the Financial sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Etienne Ricard from BMO Capital maintained a Hold rating on the stock and has a C$5.00 price target.

Etienne Ricard has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors related to Fiera’s fundamentals and risk profile. Persistent net asset outflows across both PineStone-sub-advised and other public market strategies signal ongoing challenges in generating sustainable organic growth, even as PineStone’s share of total assets continues to decline.

At the same time, the stock screens as cheap on free cash flow metrics, but elevated leverage increases earnings volatility and limits re-rating potential if performance does not improve. Reflecting weaker-than-expected assets under management and more cautious fee assumptions, he reduced his price target to $5.00, reinforcing a view that upside is constrained and that a neutral, Hold stance is appropriate.

data.description:
Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (Holdings), the Industrials sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst yesterday. Analyst Pei Hwa Ho from DBS reiterated a Buy rating on the stock and has a S$6.60 price target.

Pei Hwa Ho has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Yangzijiang Shipbuilding’s strong competitive position as a highly efficient private yard with a clear cost advantage over regional peers. Its established capabilities in complex, dual-fuel containerships and gas carriers, together with the successful delivery of its first LNG carrier, underpin confidence in sustained profitability and technical leadership.

He also points to visible earnings growth supported by a near-record US$22.4bn order book, planned capacity additions at Hongyuan and the potential Runze yard expansion, as well as new repair-yard contributions that diversify revenue.
